title: David Choe presents: Marvel Comics' Best, Most Hardcore, Violent, Outlaw Slobberknocker Fight Scene!
summary: David Choe joins Jim Rugg and Ed Piskor for a page-by-page reading of The Punisher #94–95, drawn by Frank Teran. The episode is direct craft genealogy: Choe names lessons in motion, bodies and composition, accepts a Slow Jams comparison, and describes Teran’s two-issue impact as a youthful career ideal. He also traces a childhood masculinity script through family and violent media, then explicitly revises it at 45 by distinguishing comic endurance from real bodies and describing discomfort with current violent work. Every graphic, sexual, offensive, commercial and disputed idea remains in the raw layer; the record separates attributed memory, critical analogy, collector claims, operational violence and unverified Marvel/The Hundreds leads.

source_notes.assessment: This is a direct in-episode critical observation accepted by Choe; it supports a comparison, not a copied-panel claim.

source_notes.assessment: This is direct first-person craft evidence and can be indexed as attributed influence.

source_notes.claim: Choe’s masculinity came from his father, Korean machismo and violent media.
source_notes.assessment: Preserve as autobiographical reflection; do not generalize Korean people or diagnose causation.

source_notes.claim: Choe became uncomfortable with violent media by age 45.
source_notes.assessment: Dated self-report of changed response; it does not imply censorship or a permanent current condition.

source_notes.assessment: His childhood interpretation and fight history are self-report, while his correction that real bodies cannot endure this is explicit.
